summary: Same pattern family — an in-place-morphing, fully-saturated rainbow field with an identical palette, brightness and quarter-strip spatial structure — but the port's animation runs ~1.5x too fast, its master repeat cycle is ~1.5x too long (19.5 s vs 13.0 s) with hue energy shifted from the 1st/2nd harmonic up to the 5th/10th, and it clamps a solid single-colour block of up to ~12% of the strip at one end in ~74% of frames.
observations: Both sides compile and run clean on every rig tried (strip 60 px default, strip 300 px, grid 16x16); no compile or runtime errors, no warnings, `wantsSensors: false` on both, and neither side exposes ANY control (probe: 'no settable controls' for orig and port).

Brightness/value model is an exact match: on the 60 px strip EVERY pixel on BOTH sides is fully saturated (sat = 1.000) with max channel exactly 50/255 on every frame sampled (400 frames x 60 px per side in the `hueflow` dump — the set of distinct max-channel values is literally {50} on both). meanBrightness avg 23.6 on both, `brightnessTrend: steady` on both, in every window from 6 s to 240 s.

Hue distribution matches: 12-bin hue histogram over 24 000 pixel samples reads orig 22.3 / 8.4 / 6.9 / 5.7 / 5.5 / 5.3 / 5.6 / 5.2 / 5.8 / 6.5 / 8.2 / 14.5 %, port 21.6 / 8.4 / 6.2 / 5.9 / 5.9 / 5.1 / 5.3 / 5.7 / 6.1 / 6.0 / 8.7 / 15.0 % — both pile ~37% of pixels into the two red-adjacent bins with a flat spread elsewhere. Colour is not a divergence axis here.

Spatial structure matches: at 60 px both sides show an exact repeating block of 15 px (a quarter of the strip) whose window slides over time, and both are resolution-INDEPENDENT — re-rendered at --pixels 300 the dominant self-repeat period is 75 px on both sides at every dumped time (t=0,1,2,3 s; match fraction 0.32-0.36 on orig, 0.35-0.36 on port). Mean spatial hue gradient is near-identical: orig 46.4 deg/pixel, port 43.4 deg/pixel.

Neither side translates: circular RGB cross-correlation of consecutive frames at --fps 40 gives a best shift of exactly 0 px on 32/32 frame pairs for BOTH sides, at t=0-0.4 s and t=3.0-3.4 s. The pattern morphs in place; all `motion` is hue evolution, not scrolling.

SPEED DIVERGENCE: the port's hue field evolves ~1.5x faster. Mean |d(hue)/dt| over a 39.9 s window sampled at 0.1 s: orig 129.8 deg/s, port 198.0 deg/s (ratio 1.53). Confirmed by the `motion` stat at every rate — 20 fps: orig 1.8 / port 2.8; 10 fps: 4 / 5; 5 fps: 7.1 / 10.8; 2 fps: 16 / 21 (ratio 1.5-1.6 throughout). Confirmed again by whole-frame autocorrelation at a 0.5 s lag: orig 0.382, port 0.135 — the port decorrelates far faster.

CYCLE-PERIOD DIVERGENCE: original repeats every 13.0 s, port every 19.5 s (ratio 1.50). Whole-frame RGB autocorrelation over a 60 s / 0.5 s-spaced dump: orig peaks 0.936 at lag 13.0 s and 0.796 at 26.0 s; port peaks 0.746 at lag 19.5 s. Independently confirmed by autocorrelation of the meanG series: 26 frames @2 fps = 13.0 s and 131 frames @10 fps = 13.1 s for orig; 39 frames @2 fps = 19.5 s and 197 frames @10 fps = 19.7 s for port.

The port also repeats LESS EXACTLY: its best self-correlation at its own period is 0.746 vs the original's 0.936 — the original returns to (nearly) the same frame each cycle, the port only approximately.

HARMONIC-CONTENT DIVERGENCE: temporal DFT of per-pixel hue (as e^{i2*pi*h}, 400 samples @0.1 s, summed over all 60 pixels) shows both sides are clean harmonic stacks but on different fundamentals and with the energy in different places. Orig: fundamental 0.075 Hz (13.33 s), strongest peaks at 0.075 Hz and 0.15 Hz (6.67 s) — a slow, broad undulation. Port: fundamental 0.05 Hz (20 s), strongest peaks at 0.25 Hz (4 s) and 0.5 Hz (2 s), i.e. the 5th and 10th harmonics — a much busier texture on a slower envelope. Spectral centroid: orig 0.407 Hz (char. period 2.45 s), port 0.621 Hz (1.61 s), ratio 1.53. This is visible directly in the waterfalls: over the same 20 s window (`phase-c`) the original draws roughly 5-6 large undulations and the port roughly 8-9 tighter ones.

EDGE-CLAMP ARTEFACT (port only): the port freezes a run of consecutive pixels to a byte-identical colour at one END of the strip in most frames. 60 px default rig, 120 frames sampled over 60 s (`census`): port has a >=3 px flat run in 88/120 frames (73%), 47 runs anchored at index 0, 39 at index 59, only 10 interior; longest run 7 px (11.7% of the strip); 447 pixel-slots total sit inside such runs. Original over the SAME frames: 8/120 frames, 19 of 20 runs interior, ZERO anchored at index 0, one at index 59, longest 4 px — those are genuine plateaus of the hue wave, not clamps.

The clamp is a normalized-coordinate clamp, not a fixed pixel count: on --pixels 300 the port's longest run is 31 px (10.3% of the strip) in 44/60 sampled frames, with 22 runs at index 0 and 21 at index 299 — the same 10-12% relative size. The original's longest run there is 18 px (6.0%) in 2/60 frames, all interior.

The clamp is not a start-up transient: over the late window t=120-149.5 s the port still shows a flat run in 45/60 frames (24 at the start of the strip, 21 at the end, longest 7 px) while the original shows 2/60, all interior.

Concrete examples of the clamp, from the `dump-track` hue table (degrees, 60 px strip): port t=1.5 s pixels 0-5 all hue 155; t=2.5 s pixels 0-6 all hue 0 (pure red); t=3.0 s pixels 0-5 all hue 312; t=7.0 s pixels 55-59 all hue 349; t=8.0 s pixels 55-59 all hue 229; t=18.0 s pixels 55-59 all hue 185. The clamped VALUE changes frame to frame, so it is an out-of-range input being pinned, not a fixed colour. The original's hue array at every one of the 23 sampled times varies smoothly right to both ends.

Steady state is fine on both sides: at --skip 120 --seconds 30 --fps 10 both are `steady`, zeroMotionFrames 0, meanBrightness 23.6, and the motion ratio is unchanged (orig 3.5 / port 5.5). Nothing decays, freezes or saturates.

Neither side is frame-rate coupled: each side's cycle period in SECONDS is constant across 2, 5, 10 and 20 fps (orig 13.0-13.1 s, port 19.5-19.7 s), so both integrate real elapsed time. The 1.5x speed gap is a genuine content difference, not an fps artefact.
Neither side uses randomness: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 produce identical statsSummary values on both sides (orig motion avg 3.6, port 5.5 at 30 s / 10 fps for seeds 7 and 1234; seed 1 matches).

Despite the slug, nothing font- or glyph-shaped is visible on either side: re-rendered on a 16x16 grid both sides draw the same thing — horizontal rainbow bands with no letterforms, no glyph geometry, and the same band structure on both. The grid lens confirms the port matches the original's spatial mapping; it adds no extra findings.

The survey (60 s @5 fps) and extended survey (240 s @2 fps) show NO mode/regime structure on either side — one continuous morphing texture throughout, with the only temporal landmark being the repeat cycle. Windows parked at t=0-13, t=26-39 and t=45-65 s all show the same character on each side (the original consistently broader/slower, the port consistently busier plus edge blocks).
feedback: Port's whole animation is ~1.5x too fast. Measured: mean per-pixel hue rate 198 deg/s vs the original's 130 deg/s over a 40 s window; whole-frame autocorrelation at 0.5 s lag 0.135 (port) vs 0.382 (orig); the `motion` stat runs 1.5-1.6x high at every fps from 2 to 20. Slow the hue evolution by a factor of ~1.5 (multiply the time term by ~0.65).

Port's master repeat period is 19.5 s; the original's is 13.0 s. Both are suspiciously close to Pixelblaze `time()` intervals — 13.107 s = time(0.2) and 19.66 s = time(0.3) — so the likely single-line cause is a time-base interval of 0.3 where the original uses 0.2. Fixing that alone would correct the cycle length; check whether it also corrects the speed, since the two errors are the same 1.5 factor in opposite directions.

Port's temporal harmonic content is shifted ~5x up. The original's hue energy sits on its fundamental (13.33 s) and second harmonic (6.67 s); the port's sits on the 5th and 10th harmonics of its own fundamental (4 s and 2 s). Visually the original draws broad, slow undulations in the waterfall and the port draws tight, busy ones — roughly 8-9 undulations per 20 s window vs the original's 5-6. Whatever multiplier turns the time base into a hue phase is too large in the port (or an extra fast term has been added on top of the slow one).

Port clamps at both strip ends: in ~74% of frames a run of consecutive pixels at index 0 or the last index all resolve to one identical colour — up to 7 px on a 60 px strip and 31 px on a 300 px strip (~10-12% of the strip either way; it scales with pixel count, so the clamp is happening in normalized coordinates). The original NEVER does this at either end across 240 sampled frames. Whatever index-derived coordinate feeds the hue is running out of range and being pinned to its limit instead of wrapping — make it wrap (or extend its domain) so the two ends stay smooth. This is the most visually obvious defect: it reads as a solid block of colour parked at the end of the strip while the middle keeps flowing.

The port's cycle also repeats less exactly than the original's (self-correlation at its own period 0.75 vs 0.94). Once the time base is corrected, re-check that the pattern returns cleanly to the same state each cycle; residual drift suggests an accumulating term rather than a pure function of a wrapped time value.

Do NOT change palette, brightness or spatial layout — those are already exact matches. Every pixel is fully saturated at value 50/255 on both sides, the hue histograms agree within ~1 percentage point per bin, the quarter-strip repeat block is identical, and both sides are correctly resolution-independent (the repeat block scales from 15 px at 60 px to 75 px at 300 px on both). Neither side has controls, so there is no control-surface gap either.
